newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper says he's no Superman.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper says he's no Superman.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper responded on Friday to critics who say he has failed to be tough enough on drugs, saying he is neither a miracle worker nor a superhero.
"I'm not Superman. We all have our limitations," Samper told reporters.

He was referring to remarks on Thursday by U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette, who hailed this week's passage of a law establishing harsher penalities for drug trafficking in Colombia but said the legislation should have been approved earlier.

Frechette, a vocal critic of drug policy under Samper, also complained to foreign journalists on Wednesday that production of coca leaf -- the raw material for cocaine -- had grown 30 percent in Colombia last year alone.

U.S. President Bill Clinton will decide next week, in an annual evaluation of the global fight against drugs, whether Colombia should remain on a list of countries subject to economic and trade sanctions because of their perceived shortcomings in the drug war.
Allegations that Samper's 1994 election campaign was financed by drug money were cited among reasons for the Andean nation's so-called "decertification" last year.
The embattled Colombian leader has said repeatedly that his government has done more than any before it to stem the flow of cocaine and heroin into the United States.
But in a tacit admission that Colombia's billionaire cocaine merchants remained extremely powerful, he said no one should ask him to perform miracles.
"Don't ask miracles of me," he said. "The (U.S.) ambassador seems to think Colombia's president can do the deeds of Superman."
